Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the questionnaire. Looping in Kimberly (privacy/legal) and Laura (data agreements) to coordinate. High level response below and a proposed MAP (mutual action plan) attached.

Quick answers: 
- Onshore fallback: yes — we support an onshore fallback pattern. We can configure routing policies so that UK-origin sessions are preferentially served by UK/EU residency nodes. If a UK Addendum is required and a node cannot be reached, requests fall back to the next compliant region per the routing policy; the design doc attached shows the decision tree and fallback telemetry. See redwood_onshore_fallback_diagram.png.
- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date CSV export (attached) that lists subprocessors and their processing regions. For this pilot we can provide a scoped subprocessor assertion for the services that will process HealthConnect traffic.
- Technical safeguards: encryption TLS1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest; KV cache residency controls are supported through namespace routing and explicit cache pinning in Dedicated/Private modes. Logging retention defaults to 90 days for hosted plans but can be extended for Dedicated and Private.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to draft a short TIA mapping note for your DPIA (covers SCC reliance + UK IDTA addendum interplay).
2) We exchange a scoped annex listing the exact subprocessors for the pilot and sign a limited addendum.
3) Run a short 2-week evidence sprint (we'll assign owners and dates in the MAP).

I'm attaching: mutual_action_plan.xlsx and redwood_subprocessors.csv. If that works I'll schedule a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the MAP and the TIA mapping.

Hi Sarah — quick technical/legal clarifications and a short TIA sketch below. Vanessa's MAP looks good.

TIA sketch (summary):
- Scope: processing of HealthConnect patient metadata for the pilot; controller-processor responsibilities remain per the DPA + UK Addendum.
- Safeguards: 
  * Encryption: TLS1.3 for transport; AES-256 with customer key rotation for at-rest in Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can bring KMIP/KMS integrations where available.
  * KV cache residency: cache namespaces can be routed to EU/UK pools; cache TTLs and prefix caching are configurable per customer. We log KV cache egress and record the region of the serving node in trace headers for audit.
  * Access controls: role-based admin access with MFA, just-in-time privileges for ops escalations, and retired-credential rotation every 90 days.
- Subprocessor attestations: We will provide a scoped CSV and an attestation letter for subprocessors that will touch HealthConnect pilot data. For any new subprocessor additions during pilot, we provide 30 days' notice.
- Logging & retention: audit logs (token-level) retained for 90 days on hosted; Dedicated/private retention is configurable; we can export logs for your SIEM for the pilot.

I attached a short draft TIA mapping PDF (inline answers to the questionnaire) and flagged two items that need procurement/legal input: liability cap carveouts for routing exceptions, and whether HealthConnect needs explicit SLA credits tied to failed-route fallbacks.

I'll send the draft TIA mapping and the filled questionnaire as a separate attachment by EOD.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
